_preregistration.question: is F104 revival, or regression to a common ignition level?
_preregistration.h_revival: compound tracks reference with a positive offset: slope ~ 1, delta > 0 at every checkpoint (F104 as written)
_preregistration.h_level: compound sits at a fixed value whatever the reference does: slope ~ 0, sd(compound) << sd(reference)
_preregistration.primary: weighted least-squares slope of compound ignition on reference ignition across checkpoints, with a 95% interval. Excludes 0 and covers 1 -> revival; covers 0 and excludes 1 -> common level; otherwise NOT DECIDABLE
_preregistration.range_gate: reference ignition must span 3.0x its own mean standard error before any slope is read -- without spread in the predictor both hypotheses predict the same scatter
_preregistration.harvested: step143000 from #103's run and step8000 from the killed replication; identical protocol and geometry, ignition is a per-run proportion, RUN is the unit (F57)
_preregistration.boundary: checkpoints are a training trajectory, not a random sample of models; this separates two readings of an existing effect and does not explain the level

gates.reason: reference ignition across checkpoints spans 0.7355 against its own noise floor 0.0348 (21.14x, gate 3.0x)

verdict: GRID: step1000 L8: ref 0.917 -> comp 0.938 (delta +0.021); step1000 L22: ref 0.917 -> comp 0.938 (delta +0.021); step2000 L8: ref 0.896 -> comp 0.870 (delta -0.026); step2000 L22: ref 0.896 -> comp 0.828 (delta -0.068); step4000 L8: ref 0.771 -> comp 0.703 (delta -0.068); step4000 L22: ref 0.771 -> comp 0.740 (delta -0.031); step8000 L8: ref 0.581 -> comp 0.397 (delta -0.184); step8000 L22: ref 0.581 -> comp 0.781 (delta +0.200); step143000 L8: ref 0.181 -> comp 0.516 (delta +0.334); step143000 L22: ref 0.181 -> comp 0.369 (delta +0.188). L8: slope +0.568 [+0.461, +0.674] over 5 checkpoints; sd(compound) 0.229 against sd(reference) 0.304; delta positive at 2/5. L22: slope +0.724 [+0.618, +0.830] over 5 checkpoints; sd(compound) 0.216 against sd(reference) 0.304; delta positive at 3/5. NOT DECIDABLE: the slopes separate neither hypothesis cleanly (level=[], revival=[]). With 5 checkpoints the interval is wide; the fix is more checkpoints spanning more reference ignition, not more seeds at the ones already measured. BOUNDARY: one model family, one radius, greedy, and the checkpoints are not independent of each other -- they are a training trajectory, so a slope across them is not a random sample of models. This distinguishes two readings of an existing effect; it does not establish what sets the level.
